content:
maria_k: quick follow-up from the RFC meeting — proposal to add an "atomic prefetch safety net" for safetensors sharded loads. sketch below, want alignment on interface and edgecases.

raj_p: high level summary? i've skimmed the doc but worried about perf regressions for small models.

maria_k: TL;DR: when warmup can't fetch all required shards within timeout X, we want a deterministic fallback that (1) returns a compatible quantized/compact shard variant if available, or (2) switches request routing to spare-node pool, but never return a partially-hydrated model to the runtime. goal: avoid silent correctness bugs from half-loaded weights.

alex_d: i like not exposing partial hydration to runtime. question: how do we define "compatible" variant? same layout but reduced precision? a different tokenizer?

maria_k: compatible = same architecture + same key ordering + a declared runtime-compatibility tag in the manifest. quantized variants must include a small shim mapping to the original dtype. manifest example: "compatibility": {"v1": ["float16","int8-q5"], "v2": ["float16"] }

chris_w: implementation detail: runtime checks manifest before mapping shards. if missing, atomic prefetch abandons and triggers fallback routing. sounds ok. but how do we avoid thundering herd on fallback pool?

raj_p: backpressure idea: exponential retry with jitter + token-bucket per-model hotstart. if tokens exhausted, mark model as degraded and route to cold-worker-serving (higher-latency pool).

alex_d: also need telemetry: `prefetch.result` = {ok|fallback|timeout|corrupt}. include `requested_shards`, `fetched_shards`, `fallback_reason`. would help tune X.

maria_k: agreed. propose we wire that into console and alert when fallback_rate > 0.1% over 1h for production models.

chris_w: tradeoff: strict atomicity simplifies correctness but may increase tail-latency for first requests. might break PLG startups with small infra. we should allow a per-customer policy: `allow_partial_hotstart: bool` default false.

raj_p: +1 for per-customer policy. add a safety timeout upper bound so we don't wait forever for gold pool to respond. also provide metrics so SRE can triage.

maria_k: on the API surface: loader API will add `HotstartPolicy` enum: `ATOMIC_BLOCKING`, `ATOMIC_IMMEDIATE_FALLBACK`, `PARTIAL_ALLOWED`. default `ATOMIC_BLOCKING`.

alex_d: for `ATOMIC_IMMEDIATE_FALLBACK`, do we still prefetch in background and swap when ready? that adds complexity with swap-in hooks and KV-cache invalidation.

maria_k: yes, background hotfill acceptable but must be explicit: swap must be atomic from the runtime's POV. we already have `kvcache.invalidate()` API — use that during swap. need to ensure prompts in-flight are unaffected.

chris_w: recommend a small state machine diagram in the RFC followup: START -> TRY_PREFETCH -> TIMEOUT -> FALLBACK_ROUTE -> RETURN -> BACKFILL -> SWAP with `kvcache.invalidate()` -> DONE. would clarify transitions.

raj_p: edge case: manifest says shard count N, but transport returns extra/less chunks (corrupt or updated ) — we should checksum verify entire shard bundle before commit. failure -> treat as corrupt -> try fallback. add `checksum` to manifest entry.

maria_k: agreed. example manifest entry: ```
"shards": [{"path": "m/part-000","size":12345,"sha256":"...","compat":["int8-q5","float16"]}]
```
checksum verification must be in prefetcher.

alex_d: testing: unit tests for 4 flows (happy path, timeout->fallback, corrupt->fallback, partial-allowed swap). can we add a small e2e with local s3 mock so CI validates behavior?

deploy-bot: CI: model-loader-tests passed (run 32s) :white_check_mark:

maria_k: perf concern: fallback to quantized variant might change output distribution. need eval gating — `compatibility` manifest must include `eval_hash` linking to a canned eval result. if fallback_evals differ beyond threshold, fail hotstart and escalate.

raj_p: ok but that requires eval artifacts stored with model bundle. storage cost increases. maybe require eval only for enterprise-level pinned models, not fast PLG ones.

maria_k: fair. we'll make eval gating optional with policy flags and default only for pinned models.

chris_w: last: migration path. propose feature-flag rollout: start with `PARTIAL_ALLOWED` default in canary region, collect metrics, then flip to `ATOMIC_BLOCKING` as ops comfortable.

maria_k: action items: (1) i'll update RFC with state machine + manifest checksum + HotstartPolicy enum; (2) alex to add telemetry schema; (3) raj to prototype backpressure token-bucket; (4) chris to draft rollout plan.

alex_d: acked, will send telemetry PR today.

raj_p: will spike the token-bucket prototype tomorrow.

chris_w: will author rollout + canary doc.

maria_k: thanks all. will post updated RFC here when done. :thumbsup:
